sections.content: How many people are "roofers, roof tilers and slaters"?

45,730 people

were counted on the census as "roofers, roof tilers and slaters" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Roofers, roof tilers and slaters cover roofs and exterior walls with felting, sheeting, slates, tiles and thatch to provide a waterproof surface.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "roofers, roof tilers and slaters" there were more men than women (99.2% compared with 0.8%).

This means "roofers, roof tilers and slaters" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled construction and building trades".

Men made up 99.2% and women made up 0.8% of "roofers, roof tilers and slaters"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "roofers, roof tilers and slaters" included:

  • bricklayers
  • scaffolders, stagers and riggers
  • groundworkers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "roofers, roof tilers and slaters" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "roofers, roof tilers and slaters", 14.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "roofers, roof tilers and slaters" was 65 years or older.

We can look at who worked as "roofers, roof tilers and slaters" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of men than women with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "roofers, roof tilers and slaters" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "roofers, roof tilers and slaters", 6.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (84% compared with 16%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (70.8%) than an employee (29.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
